steps.body: Count both groups. The number nine comes after six on the counting line, so nine names the larger group.
steps.narration: Count both groups. The number nine comes after six on the counting line, so nine names the larger group.

widget.prompt: Stars count to 6. Build the hearts, which count to 8 — then compare.

commonCounts.feedback: Six matches the stars; the hearts were counted two further.
Seven is one short — the hearts' count reached eight.

widget.missFeedback: Build all eight, then place both counts in the song: later wins.
widget.successFeedback: Eight — and eight comes later in the song than six, so the hearts have more.

predict.prompt: Stars count to 6, hearts to 8. Which group has more?
predict.reveal: Later in the counting song means more; being counted first is not an advantage.

cml.actionGoal: Pair the groups one to one, or place both numbers in the counting song, for kcm compare count.
invariants: Comparison rests on two facts that never move: pairing one to one leaves the bigger group with leftovers, and a number later in the counting song always names more — which is what kcm compare count uses.
misconceptions: Judging by how much space a group fills, by the size of the things in it, or by which number was written first.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more joined the smaller group, would the pairing come out even?

widget.prompt: The groups look close. What settles which has more?

options.label: Stare at them longer
options.feedback: Close groups stay close however long you look; counting gives the exact sizes.

options.label: Count both and compare the two last numbers
options.feedback: Correct — each count names its group's size, and the later counting word wins.

options.label: Pick the messier-looking group
options.feedback: Mess spreads things out without adding any; arrangement is not amount.

options.label: Ask someone taller
options.feedback: Height does not help — the counts decide, whoever does the counting.

options.feedback: Correct — 6 hearts against 5 stars; pairing one to one leaves hearts unmatched.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 9? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 9 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 10.
11 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 9 lands on 10.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 9: you land on 10.
widget.successFeedback: 10 — one hop forward, and one hop later in the song always means greater.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 10.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 9 means one hop, stopping on 10.
